newsitem.title: ITALY: First round of Italy welfare talks to end Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: First round of Italy welfare talks to end Tuesday.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi will meet union representatives and employers on Tuesday to end first-round welfare reform talks before a summer break, union sources said on Monday.

Prodi and other ministers in his centre-left government will meet representatives of 31 groups, including employers' body Confindustria and Italy's three main union confederations, who participated in the opening round of talks in mid-June.
Participants will draw up a written report on progress made so far and set a date for resuming negotiations in late August or early September.
"There is reason to believe that after the holidays, we can have more serene discussions," Labor Minister Tiziano Treu told reporters.

The talks, aimed at securing agreement on reducing social spending to help Italy qualify for the first round of Europe's single currency, have run into trouble over cuts to state pensions. Unions staunchly oppose cuts to state pensions.
The government aims for a reforms agreement to coincide with the presentation to parliament of the 1998 budget, which must be presented by September 30.
